name: Iberia
intro: Above terraced valleys, stone walls gather workshops, granaries, and households into watchful towns. Ships bring unfamiliar vessels to the coast while inland roads carry metal and grain. Let your communities bargain across frontiers, honor their sanctuaries, and write their own names upon the peninsula.
overview: Iberia emphasizes fortified agricultural towns linked to Mediterranean exchange. Productive farms sustain specialist crafts, while sanctuaries and commercial connections turn local prosperity into cultural influence without imagining a single ancient peninsular empire.
note: IBERIA means the Iberian peninsula, not Caucasian Iberia. This kit concentrates on eastern and southern Iberian-speaking societies, not every peninsular people. Some labels are modern archaeological names; no unified Iberian state is claimed. Native art and troop upgrades are approximations.

name: Thrace
intro: Horsemen ride between river valleys where royal halls glitter with worked silver. Beyond the vineyards, burial mounds keep the memory of powerful households. Gather allies through gifts and feasts, send light infantry through wooded passes, and make your court a meeting place for competing worlds.
overview: Thracian courts combine metalworking, ceremonial authority, and flexible infantry. Connected settlements support lavish royal patronage, while wooded landscapes favor mobile troops. Odrysian kingship provides a focus without erasing the region's independent communities and Greek coastal cities.
note: Thrace was culturally and politically diverse. Coastal Greek foundations appear as regional settlement labels, not ethnic Thracian foundations or permanently Odrysian possessions. Antiquity's ranged donors approximate javelin skirmishers rather than reproduce their equipment.

name: Scythia
intro: Wind bends the grass around wagons and grazing horses. Along the rivers, farmers and smiths meet riders whose ornaments bind predator and prey in gold. Keep your herds moving, command the open distances, and carry the wealth of exchange beneath the wide steppe sky.
overview: Scythia builds strength through pastures, mounted mobility, and exchange between herding and farming communities. Royal encampments support military production, while craft specialists preserve a distinctive visual language across a landscape that was never one uniform state.
note: Labels span forest-steppe archaeological sites and later Crimean Scythian settlements, not eight simultaneous nomadic capitals. Bilsk's identification with Herodotus's Gelonus is debated; modern site names are retained. Mounted native donors do not supply a new horse-archer model.

name: Nordic Communities
intro: Across narrow sounds, boats carry metal to farms beneath the northern light. Bronze gleams beside wool and grain, while carved ships travel over stone. Raise longhouses, maintain distant friendships, and let the rhythm of fields and waterways sustain communities long before the Viking sail.
overview: Pre-Viking Scandinavian communities combine household agriculture with maritime metal exchange. Workshops and coastal yields reward connected settlement, while burial landscapes sustain cultural memory. Bronze and Iron Age evidence is presented without importing Viking institutions or conquests.
note: Nordic is an archaeological umbrella for pre-Viking Scandinavian Bronze and Iron Age communities, not a contemporary national identity. City labels are modern names for excavated settlements from different centuries. No jarls, berserkers, or Viking longships are claimed.

name: Picts
intro: Beyond the northern firths, strongholds rise above fields and sea roads. Carved beasts and paired signs mark stones whose full meanings remain guarded by time. Build halls worthy of distant visitors, protect your communities, and give lasting form to the authority of emerging kings.
overview: Pictish strongholds anchor defensive armies and skilled workshops. Symbol carving, imported luxuries, and royal gatherings connect northern communities to wider networks. Antiquity placement is a gameplay convention for an essentially late antique and early medieval setting.
note: Pictish kingdoms were not one timeless tribe. Settlement labels include modern archaeological site names and later royal or ecclesiastical centers. Symbols remain incompletely understood; this kit does not invent translations or assume all Picts were tattooed warriors.
